# Part II: Generative and Multimodal Architectures {#part-generative .unnumbered}

> "Learning directly from raw text about images is a promising alternative."
>
> Alec Radford et al., ["Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020)

Part I built the machinery for a model that consumes tokens. This part steps off
the main text-model spine to follow a parallel track: generation when the object
is not naturally a left-to-right string. Images, audio, video, speech, and
embodied observations all force the same uncomfortable issue: the model must make
something coherent, but the thing being made may not have a single natural order.
The autoregressive language model resumes its lifecycle in Part III; the
architectures here are its siblings, not its successors.

Part II follows the architectures that grew around that pressure. @sec-diffusion
starts with denoising and flow matching, where generation is learned as a path
from noise to structure rather than as the next token in a sequence. @sec-nar-lm
brings that pressure back to language and asks what non-autoregressive and
diffusion language models gain, and what they lose when they give up the cache
and the clean serving story of autoregression. @sec-speech and @sec-multimodal
move through speech recognition, speech generation, vision-language fusion,
image generation, and video. @sec-beyond-text then widens the frame to world
models, robotics, and embodiment, where the missing ingredient is often not a
bigger model but a reliable stream of grounded experience.

The part is not a tour of media formats. It is a study of ordering. Whenever a
chapter seems to be about images, audio, or robots, ask what sequence the system
invented so the model could train, cache, sample, and be evaluated. That invented
order is the architecture.

## Part reflection

- **Covered:** Diffusion and flow matching, non-autoregressive language models, speech, multimodal fusion, image and video generation, world models, robotics, and embodiment.
- **Main concern:** Non-text domains must be forced into representations and sampling orders that make learning possible, and those choices often reappear later as serving and evaluation costs.
- **Takeaway:** Multimodal architecture is the discipline of inventing order for objects that did not arrive as token streams.
- **Open question:** Can grounded experience, robotics data, and world-model training scale with the regularity of text, or will the physical data bottleneck dominate?
